subject: Operator Responsibility & Evidence Schedule — addendum redlines
messages:
From: Patricia Lee <patricia.lee@triagecloud.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: TriageCloud Contracts <legal@triagecloud.com>, Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@healthsys.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operator handoff and evidence for private deployment — initial ask

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we scope the on-prem/VPC arrangement for our pilot, our legal and compliance teams have a couple of concrete asks so we can get an internal approval quickly:

1) Evidence deposit: we need an "escrow-like" pathway for a sealed snapshot and associated operator runbook at contract signature. Preferably the snapshot would be hashed and the hash deposited with a neutral third party, or we accept a notarized sealed snapshot delivered to an agreed custodian.

2) Operator responsibilities: explicit language that clarifies Redwood will not have ongoing remote admin access to the cluster unless there is a mutually agreed incident window. If operator activity is required for failover, we need a documented two-person approval and logging requirement.

3) KMS / key custody: define an HSM-backed KMS handback or split-key workflow; we need a short note in the Order Form on how key custody will be handled during the witness event.

4) Audit window & witness: request options for a 1-business-day witnessing window and either (a) a remote live witness + recorded attestation or (b) local notarization.

5) Timeline & deliverables: a checklist of what Redwood will provide at signing (snapshot, runbook, admin roster, verification hashes).

I attached a simple evidence template (Customer_Evidence_Template.xlsx) to show the fields our auditors expect. Can your team propose redline language we can circulate in our contract review?

Best,
Patricia Lee
Head of IT Security — TriageCloud
patricia.lee@triagecloud.com

Attachments: Customer_Evidence_Template.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12kb)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Patricia Lee <patricia.lee@triagecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator handoff and evidence for private deployment — initial ask

Patricia — thanks for the clear list. I'll coordinate internal owners and loop back with a redline proposal by early next week. High-level responses inline below; Marissa and Diego, can you weigh in on the legal/ops specifics?

1) Evidence deposit: agree a sealed snapshot + hash model is workable. Ops can produce a content-hash and we can engage a neutral custodian.

2) Operator responsibilities: we are comfortable with a carve-out that limits active remote admin. We will propose a canary/incident-access clause with explicit logging, timeboxed access, and pre-approved personnel.

3) KMS/key custody: two feasible patterns: a) customer-managed KMS with split-wrapping keys, or b) HSM escrow with key-handback steps during witnessing. We'll propose both as alternatives in the addendum.

4) Witnessing: we can offer remote witnessing (Zoom + recorded attestation) or local notary. Note internal approvals and scheduling lead time will be required for on-prem witnesses.

5) Deliverables: ops to produce a checklist + handoff artifacts. Marissa — can you draft the MSA addendum language? Diego — can you prepare the ops checklist and a short note on how we produce/verifiy the snapshot hash?

I'll prepare a one-page summary for Procurement and include a suggested timeline (draft addendum within 5 business days, witness scheduling within 10 business days after redline sign-off).

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Patricia Lee <patricia.lee@triagecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Mar 2028 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator handoff and evidence for private deployment — initial ask

Thanks Sean — quick pass from Legal below. Patricia, copying to keep you in the loop; happy to take direct redline conversation if you prefer.

Key approach we recommend: single addendum to the MSA titled "Exhibit X — Evidence & Operator Handoff." Keep the MSA core intact; the exhibit will be timeboxed and narrow in scope.

Suggested clauses (high-level snippets you can drop into review):

A. Snapshot Deposit: "Within five (5) business days of Order Form execution, Redwood will produce a sealed snapshot (read-only image of runtime artifacts) and provide the SHA-256 hash to Customer. Redwood may, at Customer's election, deposit the sealed snapshot with a mutually agreed neutral custodian or provide a notarized certificate of deposit. Access mechanisms to the snapshot are governed by Section D (Witness & Release)."

B. Operator Access Carve-Out: "Redwood will not perform routine remote administrative activity on Customer-managed infrastructure. In the event of a critical incident requiring Redwood intervention, Redwood may request time-limited administrative access for a maximum of two (2) discrete sessions not to exceed four (4) hours per session, subject to Customer pre-authorization and required co-approval by Customer's designated on-site engineer. All such sessions will be logged and delivered as an auditable activity record within forty-eight (48) hours."

C. KMS and Key Handover: "Customer will retain primary control of KMS keys. Where key-handback is required, the parties will follow the HSM-handback protocol detailed in Exhibit X, which may include split-key transfer, a transit-wrapped envelope deposited with the neutral custodian, or a key-release trigger tied to a witnessed attestation event."

D. Witness & Release: "Customer may elect either remote witnessed attestation (video-recorded with ISO-standard verification checklist) or in-person notarized witnessing. Release of any sealed snapshot to Customer's environment requires (i) completion of the witness protocol; (ii) signed attestation by the witness; and (iii) cross-check of SHA-256 hash values."

Redlines: I'll draft an initial Exhibit X and attach as MSA_Addendum_draft.docx. Notes: keep indemnities and IP-related clauses unchanged; this exhibit is operational and evidentiary only.

Marissa Cole
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachment: MSA_Addendum_draft.docx (Word doc, 28kb)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Patricia Lee <patricia.lee@triagecloud.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Apr 2028 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator handoff and evidence for private deployment — initial ask

Hi all — ops runbook + verification details attached. Quick operational clarifications and next steps: 

- Snapshot process: we will create a read-only filesystem snapshot (exported tarball), compute SHA-256 and SHA-512 checksums, and provide an MD5 for legacy tools if required. Snapshot will be encrypted at rest with AES-256 and transferred to the neutral custodian using SFTP with mutual TLS.

- Witnessing options: (1) Remote: live Zoom session with screen share of the export and real-time hash verification; recorded session stored with the custodian for 1 year. (2) Local notarization: Redwood engineer and Customer sign a notarized attestation at the witness event; custodian receives the sealed copy. Both options include a short operator-runbook handoff PDF and an admin roster.

- Logs & access: any remote admin session uses jump-host with session recording (ttyrec) and syslog push to an agreed collector. We'll deliver the session recording plus parsed activity log within 48 hours.

- Timeline: Ops can produce the snapshot and checklist within 3 business days of the addendum signature. Scheduling witness events: 7–10 business days lead time (remote) / 10–15 business days (in-person), depending on timezone and custodian availability.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to circulate Exhibit X redline.
2) Sean to confirm preferred witness option for TriageCloud and target signature date.
3) Once signed, ops will schedule snapshot window and send pre-witness checklist.

I've attached: ops-runbook.pdf and snapshot-proof-checklist.md.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
diego@redwood.ai

Attachments: ops-runbook.pdf (PDF, 42kb); snapshot-proof-checklist.md (text, 6kb)
